`urbanwelfare` implements the sufficient-statistics methodology of Allen, Fuchs, Ganapati, Graziano, Madera, and Montoriol-Garriga (2026, *"Urban Welfare: Tourism in Barcelona"*). Given an initial bilateral spending matrix, workplace/ownership links, and a localized demand shock, it recovers neighborhood nominal income growth, living-cost changes, and money-metric resident welfare without unit price indices or parametric preferences.

## Five-Step Workflow on Built-In Gravity Data

```{r}
library(urbanwelfare)

# 0. Load built-in 160-tract synthetic city
data(sim_city_160)

# 1. Validate two-sector open-city account & build network operators (Gamma_v, Omega^v, M)
acct <- urban_account(
  spending_base  = sim_city_160$E_R0,
  commuting_base = sim_city_160$H_0,
  origins        = sim_city_160$origins,
  destinations   = sim_city_160$destinations
)
summary(acct)

# 2. Construct direct & network-propagated exposures: F^y = (I - M)^(-1) d, F^v = Gamma_v F^y
exposures <- build_exposures(
  account     = acct,
  shock_panel = sim_city_160$shocks,
  design      = "direct",
  center_dest = TRUE
)

# 3. Step 1: Bilateral spending regression (pair & period FE, two-way clustering)
fit <- estimate_bilateral(
  panel     = sim_city_160$bilateral_panel,
  exposures = exposures,
  estimator = "ols"
)
print(fit)

# 4. Steps 2 & 3: Producer price shares (kappa^S_g), open-city common shift (c_t), & welfare
welf <- recover_welfare(
  fit          = fit,
  account      = acct,
  price_shares = "estimate_by_group",
  level_anchor = "open_city_factor_balance",
  se_method    = "bootstrap",
  n_boot       = 100,
  seed         = 42
)
summary(welf)
```

## Comparing Sufficient-Statistics Recovery to Ground Truth

Because `sim_city_160` comes from a known nonlinear spatial equilibrium, we can compare our non-parametric first-order welfare estimates directly against true nonlinear resident welfare in the peak demand period:

```{r}
truth_lp <- sim_city_160$truth$welfare_peak_lp
cat(sprintf(
  "True mean welfare: %.2f lp | Recovered: %.2f lp | Cross-tract r = %.4f\n",
  weighted.mean(truth_lp, sim_city_160$origins$pop),
  welf$headline$mean_welfare_lp,
  cor(welf$tract_summary$welfare_lp, truth_lp)
))

plot(welf, type = "decomposition")
```
